scope: Fresh validation review of shared photo recovery and bundled/local photo visibility through rapid navigation, rotation, retries and memory pressure
test_changes: Added test/review/photo_resume_bundle_rereview_test.dart with three combined visibility/recovery/resource cases

fresh_cases.name: mixed bundled local and remote reader survives hidden replacement rotation and repeated return
fresh_cases.fixture: Actual AlbumReaderSinglePageView with instrumented bundled assets, browser AssetEntity memory photos, remote preview failures and valid originals; maintained below an opaque Navigator route
fresh_cases.actions: Three hide/return visits, each with three rapid data revisions and orientation changes while hidden
verified: TickerMode is false beneath the covering route
Neither asset-bundle reads nor remote cache-manager loads increase while hidden
Each return completes preparation and shows photo pixels
After closing and cache clearing, all tracked ui.Image handles are disposed; pending/live image counts and transient callbacks return to zero

fresh_cases.name: shared recovery survives pressure during signing with a fresh URL and rapid retry
fresh_cases.actions: Two consumers initially fail, one is hidden; eight retry clicks start one pending renewal. Clear metadata during signing and join reader preparation, then complete signing, return the hidden consumer and repeat five hide/resume cycles
verified: Exactly three signing calls: initial, automatic renewal, explicit retry
Exactly one failed image load and one successful recovery load
Visible consumer, preparation and resumed consumer share the result
No retry controls remain; tracked image handles and pending/live cache entries are released after closing

fresh_cases.name: shared recovery survives pressure during signing with the same URL and rapid retry
fresh_cases.actions: Repeat the pressure/signing/preparation/visibility combination with the renewed URL string unchanged
verified: Same three signing calls and two bounded transport/decode loads
Both consumers display the recovered photo after return
Repeated visibility changes do not add requests
Tracked handles/cache entries and transient callbacks return to zero after cleanup

reviewed: Activity gates precede local provider creation and resumed shared-result adoption; ordinary scrolling does not run adoption scans
Adoption checks bounded source choices and scoped failure/recovery generations; no cache-wide scan or polling is introduced
Known decoded recoveries preserve same-URL identity, while newer failures and obsolete callbacks remain guarded
The recovered source is first and remaining fallback candidates stay reachable
Success/failure/URL metadata retains the established 500/1000/500 caps, expiration rules and pressure cleanup; entries contain no image bytes or widget/context references
Weak cache-manager IDs, temporary image stream observers and local visibility observers preserve their existing release paths
Decoded image/reader texture limits and original print rendering are unchanged

limits: Review and regression tests only; no production code changes were made.

New network cases use controlled signing and cache-manager fixtures with real Flutter image decoding; existing related tests also cover real CacheManager/HttpFileService using MockClient, not live production HTTP.
Requests that began before hiding may finish; the policy prevents starting new hidden work rather than cancelling a shared request used by a visible consumer.
No additional missing-photo state, duplicate request or persistent tracked image-handle leak was reproduced within these cases. This does not establish the absence of all native leaks or frame drops.
Physical-device frame time, peak process memory and real Android/iOS photo-library plugin behavior were not profiled; local AssetEntity coverage here uses BrowserPhotoAsset.
